identity.title: Make pipeline rename delete and active-pointer updates recoverable

origin.kind: shared GPT Pro review confirmed by source inspection
origin.summary: The shared review reported non-atomic Pipeline rename/delete and active-pointer persistence. Current Dev serializes XML atomically but sequences lifecycle file mutations without rollback or recovery and writes the active name directly.

state.current_summary: The final current-source combined WPF smoke passed all four applicable lifecycle targets, including the rendered recovery-status target after the test-harness cleanup change.

claims.text: Pipeline rename and delete can leave XML files and the active Pipeline pointer inconsistent when an intermediate file operation fails.
The active Pipeline name is written directly rather than through the repository's atomic temporary-file replacement pattern.

problem.impact: A storage or process failure can make the selected Recipe reopen with a stale or missing Pipeline identity and require manual recovery.

criteria.text: Active Pipeline pointer writes are atomic and validated against existing Pipeline inventory.
Rename and delete either complete all intended file/pointer changes or recover to one valid prior state after every injected intermediate failure.
Startup detects and repairs or explains any retained incomplete lifecycle state without deleting an operator Pipeline silently.
Normal duplicate, rename, delete, active selection, Recipe reopen, and clean-runtime checks pass with no Preview/Run, layer, or routing side effects.

context.location: Recommended model: gpt-5.6-luna | Reasoning effort: medium
Prefer atomic files plus rollback or a tiny journal; do not add a database for this desktop file store.

evidence.observation: TryRenamePipeline calls Save for the new name, File.Delete for the old name, and SaveActivePipelineName last; TryDeletePipeline deletes the XML before updating an active pointer that may reference it. Neither path has rollback or recovery state.
SaveActivePipelineName creates the directory and calls File.WriteAllText directly, while SerializeHelper.SaveXmlFile already demonstrates the repository's temporary-file replace pattern for XML.

Pipeline rename/delete now persist a lifecycle journal and validated rollback backup, recover or adopt only a proven valid state, write the active pointer through atomic temporary-file replacement, reject pointer names outside the current valid Pipeline inventory, and expose LifecycleRecoveryRequired/LifecycleRecovered states without silently deleting uncertain files.

The current focused contract injected six rename stages and five applicable delete stages, cleared runtime persistence state, re-entered through LoadActivePipelineName, and passed every case with either byte-identical prior-state rollback or proven completed-state adoption; no lifecycle journal, backup, or atomic temporary file remained.

The same current contract passed atomic active-pointer replacement, rejected a missing inventory target while preserving the existing pointer, and passed duplicate/rename/delete/active-selection/Recipe-reopen round trip on a storage-only path with no Preview/Run, layer, or route mutation.

After the current solution build, recipe change-safety, recipe context-switch, and direct-teaching Pipeline-persistence WPF targets all passed current-source quiet offscreen rendering and their no-side-effect assertions.

The final Debug solution build passed with zero warnings/errors; readiness, documentation index, and public sample checks passed. The external-reference technical check exited 0 while retaining the known PL-0005 BLOCKED DLL license/provenance rows.

The current WPF target injected an interrupted rename, reopened Recipe Manager, visibly rendered the localized 'Pipeline 변경 복구 완료' status, verified the clean prior Pipeline/journal state, and confirmed no Preview/Run, layer, document, or route mutation.

The final combined current-source WPF smoke passed recipe change safety, recipe context switch, direct-teaching Pipeline persistence, and Pipeline lifecycle recovery; each produced a 1600x900 current image with check=OK, and the lifecycle image visibly contains the localized recovered-state banner.

events.summary: Resolved after implementation and current-build evidence passed all four acceptance criteria.
